raw_response:
I will start from what I did last year and adjust a little, not too much. I have 16.1 mu total, and with well water I do not fear drought as much as dryland people, so I will keep the main land in wheat-maize because that is still the steadiest way for me to get grain. Cotton can still make money, but it takes more labor and more spraying, and my family has people working off-farm, so I will not put too much land into it. I will keep about 12 mu in wheat-maize rotation and 4.1 mu in cotton. My way is simple: wheat must not be short of base fertilizer, maize must not be short of nitrogen around the big bell mouth stage, and cotton must not be short of potash and water when setting bolls. I watch costs, but I do not save fertilizer to the point of losing yield. If I am unsure, I follow what worked in my own field and what the better growers around me did. This year I will use improved wheat seed, hybrid maize seed, and a better cotton variety, keep ploughing for wheat and cotton, use rotary tillage after wheat for maize, irrigate on time from the well, and spray when pressure shows up instead of waiting too long.
